findings.evidence: Line 425-426 `@[simp] lemma ofLiteratureT_apply ... := (rfl)`; line 429 "This is not a `simp` lemma: its left-hand side is rewritten by `ofLiteratureT_apply`"; line 225-227 `coe_qSq` is explicitly not simp.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `ofLiteratureT_apply` (keep it as the plain characteristic/apply lemma) and tag `ofLiteratureT_qSq` `@[simp]` instead, so goals normalize to `f K.tMom` on an actual transition.
findings.issue: `@[simp] ofLiteratureT_apply` rewrites `ofLiteratureT f q` to `f (-(q : ℝ))` unconditionally, so with `coe_qSq` deliberately non-simp the normal form on kinematics is the hybrid `f (-(↑K.qSq))`, and `ofLiteratureT_qSq` can never fire — its own docstring (line 429) says so. The annotation defeats the abstraction the module exists to provide.

findings.evidence: Lines 139, 164, 169 give only the `t`-forms; line 234 is the sole `_add_qSq` restatement; `coe_qSq` (line 227) is the only bridge and is non-simp by design.
findings.fix: Add the missing parallel lemmas, at minimum `tMom_eq_neg_qSq : K.tMom = -(K.qSq : ℝ)` (equivalently `minkowskiProduct_delta_self_eq_neg_qSq`) and `minkowskiProduct_p_pPrime_eq_add_qSq`, matching the shape of the existing `minkowskiProduct_avgMomentum_self_eq_add_qSq`.
findings.issue: The Q²-form of the characteristic products is given only for `⟪P,P⟫ₘ` (`minkowskiProduct_avgMomentum_self_eq_add_qSq`). There is no Q²-form for `⟪Δ,Δ⟫ₘ = -Q²`, `⟪p,p'⟫ₘ = M² + Q²/2`, `⟪p,Δ⟫ₘ = Q²/2`, `⟪p',Δ⟫ₘ = -Q²/2`. Since `coe_qSq` is not `simp`, every downstream use in the declared variable must hand-chain `tMom_def` and `coe_qSq`, including for `Δ²`, which §1.2's tensor structure `Δ^μ Δ^ν - g^{μν} Δ²` needs directly.

findings.evidence: `upstream/Physlib/.../Boosts/Generalized.lean:258` `@[simp] lemma generalizedBoost_apply_fst (u v : Velocity d) : generalizedBoost u v • u.1 = v.1`; the PR's new `Velocity.zero_spatialPart` is `@[simp]`; grep for the name finds only its definition (line 30), its docstring (line 18) and one use (line 51).
findings.fix: Delete it and close the step inline in `exists_mem_restricted_spatialPart_smul_eq_zero` (`simp` suffices), or keep only if a use outside this file is intended.
findings.issue: `spatialPart_generalizedBoost_smul_eq_zero` is public API that is closed by `simp` from two existing `@[simp]` lemmas and is used exactly once, at line 51 of the same file. It adds a name to an upstream-eligible module without adding content.

summary: The surface is mostly well-shaped (bodies hidden, `*_def` lemmas via `(rfl)`, `@[ext]` derivable, no compatibility artifacts), but one simp annotation fires against the module's own stated normal form, the Q²-side of the characteristic product API is incomplete, and one new public lemma is a single-use `simp` wrapper.
